sources.title: English language arts and literature
supports: Grades 4–6 apply grammar, spelling, and punctuation in written communication.
The curriculum includes reading, writing, listening, speaking, viewing, and representing.

sources.title: Alberta K–12 ESL Proficiency Benchmarks: Grades 4–6
supports: Grades 4–6 writing observations include pronouns, verb tense, plurals, word order, and subject–verb agreement.
Scaffolding and explicit instruction may be appropriate for learners developing academic English.

sources.authority: Government of Canada, Language Portal of Canada
sources.title: subject
supports: A complete sentence has a subject and a predicate.
An imperative sentence normally has the understood subject you.

sources.authority: Government of Canada, Language Portal of Canada
sources.title: predicate
supports: A predicate contains the verb and says something about the subject.
A predicate may also contain modifiers and complements.

sources.authority: Government of Canada, Language Portal of Canada
sources.title: Recognizing clauses
supports: A clause contains a subject and a predicate, unlike a phrase.
A direct command may have an understood subject.

sources.authority: Government of Canada, Language Portal of Canada
sources.title: The structure of a sentence
supports: Sentence length does not determine whether a sentence is complete.
A simple sentence contains one independent clause.

sources.authority: Government of Canada, Language Portal of Canada
sources.title: fragment, sentence fragment
supports: A sentence fragment does not express a complete thought.
Fragments may lack a subject or verb or may be dependent clauses or phrases.

sources.title: William Caxton
supports: William Caxton is thought to have brought the printing press to England.
The National Archives dates the first item printed in England by Caxton to 1476.

sources.title: The Printer
supports: Printing technology emerged in China centuries before it appeared in Europe.
Printing spread through workshops in multiple regions rather than beginning in England.

sources.authority: British Library Archives and Manuscripts Catalogue
sources.title: Add MS 5151: Collections for a history of printing in England, Scotland and Ireland
supports: The collection contains papers, letters, memoranda, drafts, amendments, and printer-related records.
The catalogue documents later handwritten correction and copying within collections about printing history.
